english.notes:
(i) If a company uses a name in contravention of this section an offence is committed by the company, and every officer of the company who is in default (section 1198B(5) of the Companies Act 2006).
(ii) A person has a 'relevant relationship' with a company if the person is an officer or a member of the former company (section 1198B(4)). It is irrelevant whether the person has, or has had, a relevant relationship with both companies at the same time (section 1198(3)).
(iii) Section 1198B(1) does not prevent the use by a company of a name if -
(a) it is registered under this Act by that name,
(b) the period for complying with the direction or order has not yet expired, or
(c) the direction was given, or the order was made, before section 26 of the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 came fully into force, (section 1198B(2)).
(iv) A direction under section 76B(1)(b) of the Act is not a relevant direction for the purposes of this section if given on the basis that, at the time at which a company's name was registered, the Secretary of State had proper grounds for forming the opinion mentioned in section 57A (section 1198B(7).
(v) Civil financial penalties may be issued by the registrar for this offence being a ‘relevant offence’ as defined by section 1132A of the Companies Act 2006. No criminal proceedings may be commenced against a person in respect of conduct amounting to an offence if the person has already been given a financial penalty by the registrar. Further, no financial penalty may be imposed on a person in relation to conduct amounting to an offence if proceedings in respect of that offence are ongoing or the person has been convicted.
